stem: A mobile game's DynamoDB table uses the player's country code as its partition key, and players in one country generate the overwhelming majority of traffic; the table is now throttling write requests even though its total provisioned write capacity has headroom left.

choices.text: Switch the table from provisioned capacity to on-demand mode, keeping the same partition key
Redesign the partition key around a higher-cardinality attribute, such as player ID
Increase the table's provisioned write capacity units further
Add a global secondary index on the country code attribute to speed up queries

rationale: A partition key with far too few distinct, evenly used values concentrates traffic on a single physical partition, so redesigning it around a high-cardinality attribute like player ID is what actually spreads the load and removes the hot partition. Switching billing modes changes how capacity is purchased, not how traffic is distributed across partitions, so the same key still concentrates traffic on one partition. Raising total provisioned capacity does not help when the table already has unused headroom; the problem is concentration, not total capacity. A secondary index on the same low-cardinality attribute inherits the same hot-key concentration rather than fixing it.
